newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says on track for EU membership.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says on track for EU membership.

text.p: Turkey said on Monday it was on the way to joining the European Union after EU foreign ministers at the weekend recognised Ankara's European credentials.
"A new door has opened...Turkey has been put on the track for full membership of the European Union for the first time," Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller told a news conference.
The European ministers said Turkey could one day qualify to join the European club, dispelling Turkish fears that it would never be considered for membership.
"Turkey is...recognised as having a European future," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Sunday summing up the ministers' view after talks in the Netherlands.

Ciller acknowledged that Turkey, struggling with economic woes and human rights problems, had a long way to go. "This does not mean that all-out efforts will end, to the contrary they are just beginning," she said.

Leaders of Christian Democrat parties angered Ankara earlier this month by ruling out Turkish EU membership. The leaders included German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose-Maria Aznar and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

A threat by Turkey to veto the eastward expansion of NATO unless it were given assurances of EU membership had upset many Western leaders. Ciller said Turkey could reconsider blocking NATO if the EU continued to strengthen links with Turkey.
"We will be able to come to the point of playing a more positive role in the expansion of NATO," she said.
